name: Steeg
kurzbeschreibung: Village in the upper Lechtal with the Naturpark Tiroler Lech and untouched river landscape.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Steeg is situated in the Tyrolean district of Reutte (Außerfern) at an elevation of 1,122 metres above sea level, forming the westernmost and highest municipality of the Lechtal valley on the border with Vorarlberg. Cradled between the Lechtal Alps and the Allgäu Alps along the upper reaches of the River Lech, the village is home to around 670 residents. In addition to the main village of Steeg, the municipality encompasses charming hamlets such as Hägerau, Dickenau, Prenten, and Walchen, as well as the high-altitude Walser settlements of Lechleiten and Gehren above 1,500 metres. Renowned as the cheese-making hub of the valley, Steeg is also the official starting point for the Tyrolean section of the European Lechweg long-distance trail. In winter, visitors benefit from immediate proximity to the Ski Arlberg ski area via Warth-Schröcken, while enjoying the serene, unhurried atmosphere of an authentic alpine village year-round.

Geschichte

Steeg was first recorded in historical archives in 1427. Its name derives from a fortified wooden footbridge ('Steg') that historically spanned the river gorge at this narrow crossing. A unique chapter in cultural history is the settlement of the high sunny slopes of Lechleiten and Gehren: beginning in the 14th century, Alemannic Walser settlers migrated from the Swiss canton of Valais, establishing autonomous farmsteads whose dialect and timber architectural styles endure to this day. For centuries, Steeg served as the uppermost gathering station for timber rafting along the Lech: logs felled in steep tributary gorges were cast into the torrent during the spring snowmelt and bound into rafts. The Catholic parish church of Saint Oswald assumed its current late-baroque appearance through expansions in 1786/87, featuring an ornate baroque high altar created around 1700 (originally from Oetz in the Ötztal) and a bronze portal relief ('The Last Supper') crafted in 1972 by sculptor Jos Pirkner. In the hamlet of Hägerau, the picturesque chapel of Saints Sebastian and Roch stands as a revered landmark.

Anreise

By car, Steeg is reached from the north via Reutte along the Lechtalstraße B198 running up the length of the valley (roughly 60 kilometres). From the west, year-round toll-free access is provided through Vorarlberg and the Bregenzerwald via the L200 road through Schoppernau to Warth, connecting directly to the B198 down into Steeg. In summer, the mountain pass of Hahntennjoch (L246) offers a scenic route from Imst in the Inntal valley. Rail travellers arrive at Langen am Arlberg or St. Anton am Arlberg stations on the main Arlberg railway, or at Reutte in Tirol station. VVT regional bus route 110 runs hourly linking Steeg with all Lechtal communities through to Reutte and on to Warth. In winter, complimentary ski buses transport winter sports enthusiasts directly to the Arlberg cable cars at Warth.

Tipps

A culinary must is visiting Naturkäserei Sojer in the village centre: established in 1903, this artisan show dairy processes fresh, silage-free Lechtal hay milk into award-winning alpine hard cheeses, semi-hard cheeses, and farmhouse butter, complete with tastings and a farm shop. For leisure and relaxation, the Aqua Nova adventure indoor pool features a sports pool, 60-metre flume slide, and expansive wellness sauna area. In the hamlet of Hägerau, visitors can enjoy natural Kneipp pools beneath the Hägerau waterfall and admire the thundering, 80-metre-tall Schreitenbach waterfall. As a key station of the Lechweg, Steeg offers magnificent high-altitude walks towards Lechleiten or downriver towards the spectacular Holzgau suspension bridge. In winter, a ten-minute drive connects skiers to Austria's largest interconnected ski area, Ski Arlberg, offering more than 300 kilometres of pistes.
